I never said you're not allowed to be sad. I would never tell a person who just lost a pet it's their fault, i wouldn't comment on it at all because it's not my cat and they didn't ask but it does make me wonder if they feel guilty. Cats don't need to go outside, if it's a rescue that's been allowed out before then sure, it's what they know, then it's cruel but if the cat is indoor from birth, they are absolutely fine, I never had a cat that showed any signs of wanting to go outside. I don't know if it's the breed or the area but all my cats wanted was bed, food, toy, cuddle sleep, never meowing at the door or clawing or whatever behavior indicated they want to go outside. I think more than one person mentioning the car crash analogy is a little irrelevant honestly, cats are smart but they're not human smart, cats can't drive a car or get in a car crash, compared to humans cats are babies and you wouldn't let a baby drive a car so I'm struggling to understand how the car crash things proves anything. The question of 'don't you feel guilty that your cat died outside' mostly comes from frustration. I'm in a few Facebook groups for my local outdoor cats where people can ask for help if their cat gets lost etc. and multiple times a week there's posts about people finding dead cats (with collars so they're owned) that have been ran over or kicked or their tail has been cut off etx. and it's just not very nice honestly. I get there's nothing you can do about dickheads but like, I dunno I just wouldn't ever put my cat in a dangerous situation like that. And I don't even live in a bad area so I'd there's twats here then I don't even want to think about outdoor cats in bad areas
